findings.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `url` is interpolated unescaped into an `<a href>` tag and stored with `cook_method: raw_html`, bypassing the sanitizer; a single-quote in the embed_url (e.g. `http://host/x'onmouseover='alert(1)`) yields stored XSS. Needs `ERB::Util.html_escape` on both occurrences.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35-36 — feed item HTML is passed through `CGI.unescapeHTML` and imported as `raw_html` with no sanitization, so any script/iframe/event handler in a third-party feed is rendered verbatim to all users.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:47 and app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:30 — `open(url)` is `Kernel#open`, not `URI.open`; a value starting with `|` executes a shell command and a non-URL value reads a local file. `import_remote` should require an http(s) scheme before opening.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:16 — unauthenticated users can make the server fetch any path on `embeddable_host` via a spoofed Referer, and open-uri follows redirects so a redirect can reach internal addresses (SSRF); no timeout or size cap on the fetch.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:20-30 — race condition: two concurrent imports of the same URL both see `embed.blank?`, both run `PostCreator#create` (enqueuing jobs/side effects), then the second `TopicEmbed.create!` hits the unique index and raises; the transaction rolls back rows but not enqueued jobs/notifications.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 items that only carry `<description>`, so `.scrub` raises `NoMethodError` and aborts the whole poll; `String#scrub` also requires Ruby 2.1+.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:78 — `topic_id_for_embed` does an exact string match on `embed_url` while values come from two sources (page JS vs feed link/id), so trailing slash, scheme, or query string differences cause a miss and create duplicate topics for the same article.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:38-41 — `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs the full feed download and import synchronously inside every uncached embed request's job, in addition to the hourly schedule, with no lock against the scheduled run.
lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-30 — `setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is not atomic; a crash between them leaves `retrieved:<url>` without a TTL, permanently throttling that URL for non-staff.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — origin check uses a substring test (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`), so `http://forum.example.co` passes for `http://forum.example.com/`; origins should be compared exactly.
app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — `<%- end if %>` is a typo that only works by accident because the appended string is truthy; should be `<%- end %>`.
app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:27 — `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid value and only works because browsers ignore it; the header should be deleted instead of set to a bogus value.

app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8-10 — the page reloads every 30 seconds forever, even when retrieval can never succeed (wrong host, missing embed_by_username, 404), hammering `/embed/best` from every open tab.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string; a frozen or reused string (e.g. the disqus import) will raise or accumulate footers.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `url` is interpolated unescaped into an `<a href>` tag and stored with `cook_method: raw_html`, bypassing the sanitizer; a single-quote in the embed_url (e.g. `http://host/x'onmouseover='alert(1)`) yields stored XSS. Needs `ERB::Util.html_escape` on both occurrences.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, `url` is only checked with `/^https?\:\/\//`, so a value like `http://host/x'onmouseover='alert(1)` passes. That `url` is then interpolated directly into an HTML string (`"#{url}"`) appended to `contents`, and the created post is saved with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Post#cook returns `raw` for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline, and the embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This makes the unescaped interpolation a verifiable stored-XSS vector via breaking out of the single-quoted href attribute (and also affects the link text). Escaping/sanitizing the URL (and/or avoiding raw_html) is needed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35-36 — feed item HTML is passed through `CGI.unescapeHTML` and imported as `raw_html` with no sanitization, so any script/iframe/event handler in a third-party feed is rendered verbatim to all users.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the feed item body is taken from `i.content` and passed through `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then into `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates the post with `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`. `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. As a result, any HTML (including `<script>`, event handlers like `onerror`, iframes, etc.) coming from a third-party feed can be stored and rendered as-is (and the embed view also uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>`). This is a verifiable XSS/security issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:16 — unauthenticated users can make the server fetch any path on `embeddable_host` via a spoofed Referer, and open-uri follows redirects so a redirect can reach internal addresses (SSRF); no timeout or size cap on the fetch.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The `/embed/best` endpoint is publicly reachable and only gates access using `request.referer` (EmbedController#ensure_embeddable). Since Referer is a client-supplied header, an unauthenticated client can spoof it to pass the check and supply an arbitrary `embed_url` as long as its host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (enforced later by TopicRetriever#invalid_host?). When no embed exists, the controller enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, which calls `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` → `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` with no explicit timeout/size limit. Ruby's `open-uri` follows HTTP redirects by default, so a URL on the allowed host that redirects to an internal address can be used to make the server fetch internal resources (SSRF via redirect), and large/slow responses can tie up resources due to lack of caps/timeouts in this code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:20-30 — race condition: two concurrent imports of the same URL both see `embed.blank?`, both run `PostCreator#create` (enqueuing jobs/side effects), then the second `TopicEmbed.create!` hits the unique index and raises; the transaction rolls back rows but not enqueued jobs/notifications.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In TopicEmbed.import it does a non-locking lookup `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, enters a transaction that calls `PostCreator.new(...).create` and then `TopicEmbed.create!` (topic_embeds has a unique index on `embed_url`). Two concurrent callers for the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and both create a post/topic; the second will then hit the unique constraint on `topic_embeds.embed_url` and raise, causing its DB transaction to roll back. The race/exception is directly implied by the diff; and since `PostCreator#create` can have side effects outside the DB transaction, the "rolled back rows but not side effects" concern is plausible even if not fully provable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 items that only carry `<description>`, so `.scrub` raises `NoMethodError` and aborts the whole poll; `String#scrub` also requires Ruby 2.1+.
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that `i.content` may be nil for many RSS items (e.g., RSS 2.0 using only `<description>`), causing `.scrub` to raise `NoMethodError`/nil dereference and break polling; the candidate additionally notes a Ruby version requirement but the core issue matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:78 — `topic_id_for_embed` does an exact string match on `embed_url` while values come from two sources (page JS vs feed link/id), so trailing slash, scheme, or query string differences cause a miss and create duplicate topics for the same article.

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` performs `where(embed_url: embed_url)` (exact string match). In this diff, `embed_url` can come from multiple sources with no normalization: (1) the embedding JS passes `discourseEmbedUrl` verbatim to `/embed/best?embed_url=...`, and (2) feed polling imports `i.link` or `i.id` as the URL, and `import_remote` uses the passed URL as-is. Since `TopicEmbed.import` and `TopicRetriever` also key existence checks on the raw `embed_url` string, any equivalent-but-not-identical URL forms (http vs https, trailing slash, query params, different feed id vs link) will miss the lookup and can result in creating a new topic/embed row for the same article. The unique index only prevents exact duplicates, not canonical duplicates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:38-41 — `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs the full feed download and import synchronously inside every uncached embed request's job, in addition to the hourly schedule, with no lock against the scheduled run.

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` the code does:

```ruby
if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?
  Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})
  return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?
end
```

So whenever an embed URL is requested and no existing `TopicEmbed` exists yet, the *entire* `PollFeed` job is executed synchronously as part of that retrieval flow (which itself runs in `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`). This duplicates the scheduled hourly `Jobs::PollFeed` and there is no locking/mutual exclusion around feed polling, so multiple `RetrieveTopic` jobs (or the scheduled poll) can run `PollFeed` concurrently, repeatedly downloading/parsing the feed and attempting imports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-30 — `setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is not atomic; a crash between them leaves `retrieved:<url>` without a TTL, permanently throttling that URL for non-staff.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the code does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two distinct Redis operations; if the process crashes, is killed, or errors after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key can be left without a TTL. That would cause `setnx` to keep failing on subsequent calls, making `retrieved_recently?` return true indefinitely and permanently throttling retrieval for that `embed_url` (unless someone manually deletes the key).

matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that using `indexOf`/substring matching for origin validation is insecure and can be bypassed by crafted origins/domains that contain the expected value as a substring; they recommend exact origin comparison instead.

matched_golden_ids: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same underlying ERB/Ruby syntax issue: the template closes the block with `end if`, which is incorrect here and should be replaced with a plain `end` to properly close the `if` block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:27 — `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid value and only works because browsers ignore it; the header should be deleted instead of set to a bogus value.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the diff explicitly sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. The standard/recognized `X-Frame-Options` values are `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`, and (deprecated) `ALLOW-FROM <uri>`; `ALLOWALL` is not a valid value. Using a nonstandard value can lead to inconsistent browser behavior (often ignored), so the finding that this is a real correctness/security-header issue introduced by the diff is grounded in the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8-10 — the page reloads every 30 seconds forever, even when retrieval can never succeed (wrong host, missing embed_by_username, 404), hammering `/embed/best` from every open tab.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbedController#best` renders `loading` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, after enqueueing `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. The `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` template contains a `setTimeout` that unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds, with no stop condition. If retrieval can never create a `TopicEmbed` (e.g., `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` is blank so `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early without importing, or remote fetch/import repeatedly fails), the page will stay in the loading state and keep re-requesting `/embed/best` indefinitely from each open embed iframe/tab.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string; a frozen or reused string (e.g. the disqus import) will raise or accumulate footers.

adjudication.rationale: It’s true that `contents << ...` mutates the `contents` argument in `TopicEmbed.import`, but the finding’s claimed impact (“a frozen or reused string (e.g. the disqus import) will raise or accumulate footers”) is not demonstrably triggered by any call sites in this diff. The new callers (`PollFeed` and `import_remote` used by the Disqus task) pass freshly created strings and do not reuse them after the call, and nothing in the diff shows `contents` being frozen. So the mutation is verifiable, but the reported bug scenario is speculative and not evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 and db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — `force: true` silently drops an existing table, and editing an already-shipped migration (`create_top_topics`) has no effect on migrated databases.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, and adds a new migration `create_topic_embeds` using `force: true`. In Rails, `create_table ... force: true` will drop the table if it already exists (potentially destroying data) instead of failing. Also, modifying an already-shipped migration like `create_top_topics` will not affect databases that have already run that migration (it won’t be re-executed), so the change is ineffective for already-migrated installs if it was meant to fix something there.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:15-16 — `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` raise when a post's user has been deleted (`user` is nil).

adjudication.rationale: The new embed view dereferences `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` without a nil-guard, but the diff does not show any change that would make `post.user` nil, nor does it show that posts can exist without a user. In typical Discourse/Rails setups, `posts.user_id` is required and user deletion is handled without leaving orphaned posts (e.g., reassignment/soft-delete), so the proposed crash scenario depends on external behavior/data not evidenced in the diff.
